name: glass
description: Glass: VU meters, spectrum, turntables and reels on the player's display
author: foonerd; audio path from PeppyMeter Screensaver by 2aCD (original) and Just a Nerd

volumio_info.details: Glass draws VU meters, spectrum analysers, turntables and tape decks on the player's display from PeppyMeter themes. It is a native display, one small binary, with no Python and no browser in the path. Glass replaces PeppyMeter Screensaver: only one of the two may be enabled.
volumio_info.changelog: 0.7.4 A remote's needles and bars move as the player's own do: the frames daemon sends the frames in each hop, and the remote times its decay by the player's stamps. 0.7.3 A remote display is set up on a page of its own: its players, a theme followed or kept as its own, its window, frame rate and gain, applied while it runs; the Remotes tab links to each remote's page. 0.7.2 The status tab says whether remote displays are served, on which ports, and how many receive frames. 0.7.1 Remote displays are served only when the manager's Remotes tab says so, with the ports set there; a player with no screen of its own serves remotes without opening a window. 0.7.0 Remote displays: Glass on another machine shows this player's meters with its theme, fonts and icons; the plugin sends the frames, serves the channel over TCP, announces the player, and lists the remotes in the manager. 0.6.11 The measured line no longer calls a playing source unmeasured when the ring's stamp lands a hair ahead of the manager's clock. 0.6.10 The status tab says whether what plays is measured, from the tap's rings, so a source playing below the tap is seen at a glance. 0.6.9 Soloist Connect plays again with Glass running: it stays on the player's own device, where the tap measures it, and Glass nudges it after every rewrite of the ALSA file so a device sampled mid-start is corrected. 0.6.8 Soloist Connect meters again after a backend start: Glass tells Soloist its metering is on after every rewrite of the ALSA file, so Soloist opens the tap (plug:spotify) rather than a device read from a half-written file. 0.6.7 The settings backups an upgrade writes on its own are kept to the newest five; named backups are never touched. 0.6.6 'Open the manager here' opens it in this window, inside Volumio's page, instead of a new tab; the manager's inputs take the kiosk's on-screen keyboard. 0.6.5 The settings page sets the manager's port (the manager moves at once, and says when the port is taken) and its address for players where .local names do not resolve. 0.6.4 A settings backup downloads as a zip and a zip uploads as a backup, so settings move from one player to another. 0.6.3 The restart after an upgrade is one systemd restart job, so the backend comes back on its own. 0.6.2 The manager looks for a new release a minute after start and once a day, and says so in its header. 0.6.1 Glass upgrades itself from the manager: the latest release is checked on GitHub, its zip downloaded and verified against the release digest, the settings backed up and the installed plugin kept for going back, then the player's plugin manager replaces the plugin and the backend restarts. 0.6.0 The Glass Manager: a web application the plugin serves on its own port for everything that manages the display. Installed themes with previews the display draws itself, the theme catalog with checksum-verified installs and updates, theme uploads, the meter rotation, the artist fanart settings, settings backups and a status page. The settings page keeps what operates the display and opens the manager.
